status: measured on Anton by read only reads, including the native handshake of one controller launched worker, and on a CI runner by a kind fixture with an interrupted registry
evidence_class: Measured: two read only Anton reads (kubectl get nodes, events and Pods; aws describe scaling activities and instances) at 2026-10-11T14:57:15Z and 15:59:13Z, each covering the hour of events Kubernetes keeps; a third read at 2026-10-12T10:17:25Z added the agent log of every swarm worker Pod, holding one Pod the swarm controller launched on Anton at 10:03:14Z; two Startup stages runs (38150380291 at ec5276308, 38153743721 at f49241dc5) on GitHub hosted runners pulled the published worker image through a local registry with the committed driver, each behind a 90 second outage on both kind workers; an earlier run, 38150051995, used an older driver and is not committed. Attribution, report, claim and the account release are functions over committed reads; the account release runs the KUB-05 recovery over fakeredis and is mocked. No antoncore object, autoscaler setting or deployed Pod was changed.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.startup_stages.reduce(raw) keeps only the event reasons, node Ready transitions, Pod creation and readiness, and successful ASG launch activities joined to EC2 launch times that attribution reads; with worker logs it adds each Pod's prepared and delivered instants read by log_marks
startup_stages.log_marks(text) reads `kubectl logs --timestamps` output for the worker_start prepared report and the first supervisor prompt_delivered record after it

startup_stages.attribute(read) gives one sample per Pod with scheduling or failure evidence: node kind (cold when an instance requested after the Pod waited served it), node source (existing, new_instance, warm_pool), from_zero from the scale up that requested that instance, image cache (cached, uncached, partial, unknown), outcome (started, pending or a failure class), transient failure the Pod started past, sandbox retries, time to first failure and stages trigger, instance, join, schedule, image, pull_retry (time lost to failed pulls before the pull that succeeded), pod_start, bootstrap, handshake (the worker's prepared report to the supervisor's prompt delivery after the native agent reported ready); a Pod listed after its scheduling event is a later incarnation and its listing is ignored

startup_stages.report(samples) gives startup_stage_p50_p95 per scenario with failures, pending and transient counts beside the starts, node_provision_ms (trigger, instance, join and schedule: the Pod waiting until the new node accepts it) apart from image_init_ms (the successful pull plus failed pulls before it); the rendered page shows failures and transient failures in their own columns
startup_stages.claim(samples, cold_scale_from_zero) raises ClaimRefused naming every sample that landed on an existing node, came from a non empty pool or did not pull uncached
startup_stages.unbounded(samples, grace) lists pull failures, final or transient, classified later than the KUB-05 pull grace or never timed
python -m scripts.swarm_v2.startup_bench reduce, report and claim expose those on the command line; claim exits 2 with the refusal and writes nothing

tests/performance/swarm_v2/startup.py kind drives the kind fixture: uncached then cached worker image on each node, then every node pulling while the local registry is stopped for --outage seconds, recovery waited, capture written for reduce, and a non zero exit when a Pod is not ready, not classified within grace or not recovered; startup.py anton writes the read only Anton listings and the agent log of each Pod in the swarm workers namespace the committed reads were reduced from
.github/workflows/startup-stages.yml runs the fixture on dispatch, on call and on branch pushes touching the fixture or the startup modules, and uploads the startup-stages artifact

supported_versions.cluster: Anton k3s v1.33.12 with containerd 2.2.3 and the installed cluster autoscaler; kind v0.33.0 with node image v1.37.0 in CI
supported_versions.compatibility: New modules and a new workflow only; the local runtime and every deployed object are unchanged. The worker resources workflow now triggers only on its own workloads folder.

authority: The benchmark only reads. Anton reads used read only kubectl and aws describe calls; the kind fixture creates and deletes objects only inside its own throwaway cluster and namespace. A cold label is granted only by claim over the samples' own provenance, never by a scenario name or a caller label.
authoritative_objects: None are written. Raw listings stay outside the repository; only reduced reads with the sha256 of every listing are committed. The fixture deletes only its own namespace in its own kind cluster.

states.observed: Anton read 1: 846 samples, 845 started, 16 cold, 15 of them on the ondemand pool scaled from a non empty pool and 1 on the swarm pool scaled from zero; read 2: 598 samples, 595 started, 2 cold, 1 from zero. Kind runs: uncached worker image pulls 10.0 to 11.1 s, cached pulls 0, every interrupted pull classified registry_unavailable within the scheduling second, every interrupted Pod started after the registry returned. Read 3: 661 samples on warm nodes, one of them the swarm controller's worker Pod with a 1085 ms native handshake.
states.accepted: Case A: each fixture passes on its own: both Anton reads split node provision from image pull for every cold row and accept their from zero sample as cold_scale_from_zero; both kind runs started every sample with the uncached pull measured; the two Anton reads share no started sample, only the plane-0 pull failure continuing through both. Case B: the ondemand cold samples (from a non empty pool, or a warm pool instance), 50 warm samples and 11 cached kind samples are each refused the cold label with their reason; the claim command exits 2 and leaves its read byte identical. Case C: both kind Pods behind the 90 second outage were classified registry_unavailable one second after scheduling, the outage was charged to the image phase as failed pulls, and both started; none is unbounded. In the KUB-05 recovery an image pull holds the account slot only within the 120 s grace; past it the attempt is fenced with grant and account released, no slot remains and a replayed pass leaves fence and decision unchanged.

validation.review: Standards and Spec readers on the diff since the SV2-PRF-01 head: warm pool cold labels, failure timing, a silent fixture exit, outage time charged to the Pod phase, the image total including Pod start, the schedule stage outside node provision, hidden transient failures, a tautological repeat check and kind provenance were fixed in code; the remaining points are recorded as limitations; handshake round: Standards (5 findings) and Spec (7 findings) readers, resolution in https://github.com/the-cloud-clockwork/agentihooks/pull/2641#issuecomment-6122393601, the per container image split filed as a ledger follow up

findings: Ondemand new instances join in 36 to 37 s after EC2 launch, warm pool instances in 22 s, the swarm pool c7i-flex instances in 46 and 56 s.

On the swarm pool the Pod waited a further 75 and 96 s after the node turned Ready: the scheduler reported the Pod's node affinity or selector unmatched on the new node for that time. A node label applied after join is the likely cause; it is a hypothesis, filed as a ledger follow up.
Every ondemand cold start in read 1 hit one FailedCreatePodSandBox retry, and its Pod start ran 30 to 70 s beyond the pull.

Behind a 90 s registry outage, the four interrupted pulls across both kind runs spent 89.9, 168.6, 169.8 and 173.4 s in failed pulls before the pull that succeeded, against 10.1 to 12.6 s for the successful pull itself; that time counts in the image phase. Hypothesis, not shown: kubelet image pull back off, which grows during the outage, delays the retry past the registry's return.

The one controller launched worker on Anton (read 3) took 1.085 s from its prepared report to the prompt delivery after the native agent reported ready, inside 17 s from container start to Pod Ready; its uncached worker image pull took 19.2 s and the agent container was created 20 s after that pull ended, which the Pod start column carries.

native_handshake_samples.accepted: single observation, n 1, not a latency claim
native_handshake_samples.image_note: image is every pull the Pod made before its last container started: the 1962 ms bundle init container pull and the 19245 ms worker image pull

limitations: The native handshake has one sample: only one controller launched worker Pod ran on Anton within the hour of read 3, so its p50 and p95 are that sample; it is read from the worker's own log timestamps and falls inside bootstrap.
Anton samples are the workloads that ran in each hour, mostly CI runners and services, not swarm workers; only two swarm pool scale from zero samples exist.
Events older than an hour are gone, so each read only sees the hour before it.
EC2 launch times have one second precision.
The kind registry runs on the same runner, so its pull times reflect image size and unpack, not registry distance.
With two cold samples in read 2 the p95 equals the maximum.
The kind fixture has no cold node: a kind cluster cannot add a node, so cold node stages come only from the Anton reads, which held no registry interruption.

The committed reads keep EC2 instance ids, node names and Pod names, which identify capacity and workloads but carry no credential; the outage start and stop times live only in each run's fixture.json artifact.
rollback: Use the previous qualified image and reduce launch concurrency: this package changes no deployed image, concurrency or autoscaler setting, so its rollback is reverting the pull request. Rehearsed on 2026-10-12 in a throwaway checkout of tested commit 71a2e1285 (wt.sh tmp): `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/dev) HEAD | git apply -R --index` left `git diff --cached --stat <merge base>` empty, so the revert restores dev exactly; `git grep -l -E 'startup_stages|startup_bench' HEAD -- scripts hooks profiles` found no importer outside the package, so the revert changes no other runtime path. The previous image rollback and a concurrency reduction were not rehearsed because nothing deployed changed. The fixture showed both Pods recovering from the outage without a manual step, and the mocked recovery case shows the account slot released past the pull grace with nothing left reserved.
